t.2.22.1: Having cast off that distress and touched pure water, Rāma's mother, the high-minded lady, performed auspicious rites for him.
t.2.22.3: May the seasons and the fortnights, the months, the years and the nights, the days and the hours ever bring you well-being.
t.2.22.2: May the Sādhyas, the Viśvas, the Maruts and the great sages grant you well-being; may Dhātā and Vidhātā grant you well-being; may Pūṣan, Bhaga and Aryaman grant you well-being.
t.2.22.4: May Memory, Steadfastness and Righteousness protect you on every side, my son, and may the blessed god Skanda, and Soma together with Bṛhaspati, protect you too.
t.2.22.5: May the Seven Sages and Nārada protect you on every side, and may all the constellations and the planets together with the deities guard you as you, wise one, wander through the great forests in the garb of a hermit.
t.2.22.6: In the forest may there be no monkeys, scorpions, gadflies or mosquitoes, nor reptiles and insects, to trouble you in the dense thicket.
t.2.22.8: May the fierce eaters of human flesh, and whatever other kinds of creatures there are, not harm you, my son, for here they have been duly worshipped by me.
t.2.22.7: May the great elephants and lions, the tigers and fanged bears, and the fierce horned buffaloes never do you harm, my dear son.
t.2.22.9: May your returns be auspicious, and may your valorous deeds and all your undertakings meet with success. O Rāma, go in safety, my dear son.
t.2.22.10: May there be well-being for you, again and again, from the beings of the sky and of the earth, and from all the gods, and from those who are your adversaries.
t.2.22.11: May Brahmā, lord of all the worlds, the sustainer of beings, and likewise the seers, and those gods who remain, may they all protect you as you dwell in the forest.
t.2.22.12: Thus the illustrious, wide-eyed lady worshipped the hosts of gods with garlands and with perfumes, and with fitting hymns of praise.
t.2.22.13: The blessing that came to the thousand-eyed one, revered by all the gods, at the destruction of Vṛtra, may that blessing be yours.
t.2.22.14: The blessing that Vinatā once invoked for Suparṇa when he sought the amṛta, may that blessing be yours.
t.2.22.15: Kausalyā also made a protective charm from an auspicious, potent herb that draws out arrowheads and heals wounds, and she consecrated it by murmuring mantras over it.
t.2.22.16: Drawing him down, kissing him on the head and embracing him, the illustrious lady said: "My son, go as you please, Rāma, with your purpose accomplished."
t.2.22.17: Dear child, I shall see you come back again to Ayodhyā, free from illness, with all your aims accomplished, happily and firmly settled in the royal palace.
t.2.22.19: Speaking thus, her eyes brimming with tears, she completed the rite for his welfare according to the prescribed rule; then she walked around Rāghava, keeping him on her right, and, pressing him close again and again, she embraced him.
t.2.22.18: O Rāghava, may the hosts of gods headed by Śiva, the great seers, the spirits, the great asuras and the serpents, all worshipped by me, and the quarters too, seek your welfare as you depart for the forest for a long time.
t.2.22.20: Thus circumambulated by the queen, he pressed his mother's feet again and again, and then the greatly renowned Rāghava, blazing with his own splendour, went to the dwelling of Sītā.
